rules.statement: Don't ask a test suite to also parse or compare generated copies of the code it tests when an existing check already fails if any generated copy differs from its source by a single byte.
rules.why: The maintainer declined this: a byte-for-byte sync check between the source and its generated copies is already stricter than comparing one function in each copy.
rules.check: Before reporting that only one copy of duplicated or generated code is tested, look for a template or sync test that compares the generated files with their source. Report only if no such check exists.

rules.statement: When a test exercises only the source copy of code that a generator copies into other files, the test's header names the generator and the check that keeps the copies in sync.
rules.why: Without that note, readers assume the shipped copies are untested and could drift from the source.
rules.check: Look for a test file that loads one copy of code that exists in several generated files, and whose header does not point to the generator or the sync check.

rules.statement: When code makes a deliberate behavioral choice, such as a case-sensitive comparison, an inclusive `>=` boundary or a guard that skips input before the first section, add a test that fails if that choice is reversed.
rules.why: If no test pins the choice, changing `-cmatch` to `-match`, `-ge` to `-eq` or dropping a guard leaves the suite green while behavior departs from the documented rule.
rules.check: For each deliberate comparison mode, boundary operator or guard in the diff, check whether some test input would give a different result if the operator were flipped or the guard removed.

rules.statement: When code scans Markdown for headings, it opens a code fence on a run of three or more backticks or tildes, closes the fence only on a bare run of the same character at least as long as the opening run, and treats an unclosed fence as running to the end of the file.
rules.why: This is the Markdown fence rule. If a single flag toggles on any fence marker, mixed markers make headings inside code samples count, or real headings after the sample get skipped.
rules.check: Look for fence detection that toggles one flag on any ``` or ~~~ line, or that ignores the length of the opening run, or ignores text after the closing run.

rules.statement: Tests for Markdown fence handling cover tilde fences, each marker type inside the other, shorter or annotated runs that don't close a fence, longer runs that do, section headings inside a fence, and unclosed fences.
rules.why: Each of these branches can break without failing a test that uses only a closed backtick fence.
rules.check: Check whether the fence-handling tests include only a closed backtick fence, and whether any of the listed cases is missing.

rules.statement: A new changelog entry follows the wording of earlier entries of the same kind, including any closing sentence that tells consumers how to pick up the change.
rules.why: If the entry leaves out the usual pickup instruction, readers may not know they must take an action to get the feature.
rules.check: Compare a new changelog entry with earlier entries of the same kind, and look for a closing sentence the earlier entries share that the new one leaves out.
